name: Generate reference data by performing and recording actions
description: The process of deliberately performing known actions on a system and recording exactly what was done, how and when, so that the record is ground truth for the traces those actions leave.
details: Each recorded action is one piece of ground truth, for example "file A copied to B by byte copy, between 10:02:03.120 and 10:02:03.141 on the recording host's clock". Record the exact method used (system call, command or user-interface gesture), since different methods leave different traces, and the environment (operating system, version, drivers, hardware) and clock. The technique is commonly the first part of DFT-1090, followed by preserving the resulting data (DFT-1110, e.g. imaging the system) and analysing the traces; it is also used to build test data for tool testing and datasets, where the behaviour is already known. Its output is the record of the actions, not a conclusion about what traces they leave: working out which traces came from which action is part of DFT-1090.
examples: Building a test image for tool testing by performing a planned sequence of file system operations on a test volume, recording each with its method, start and end times
Building a labelled dataset by performing scripted user-interface actions on an app in a virtual machine, each action recorded as it is performed
Automatically exercising an app after each update to generate reference data [DFCite-1034]

references.relevance_summary_280: Generates reference data automatically by performing app actions after every update, recording what was done: an example of generating ground truth at scale.
